svg.title: Carrier Size Threshold Ladder
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-carrier-size-threshold-ladder; chapter number: 2; title: Carrier Size Threshold Ladder; subtitle: The inch lines where additional handling, oversize, and over-maximum fees start; chart type: horizontal_bars; unit: inches; bars: label: Additional Handling 30-Inch Trigger; min: 30; max: 30; typical: 30; display: 30 in; label: Additional Handling 48-Inch Trigger; min: 48; max: 48; typical: 48; display: 48 in; label: FedEx Length Limit to Variance; min: 96; max: 98; typical: 97; display: 96 in limit; 97 in product; 98 in negotiated variance; label: Oversize Length Plus Girth Line; min: 130; max: 130; typical: 130; display: 130 in length plus girth; 90 lb minimum billable weight; label: UPS Over-Maximum Line; min: 165; max: 165; typical: 165; display: 165 in length plus girth; $1,325 per package; caption: Invoices price on billable weight, the greater of scale and dimensional weight, and surcharges now drive spend: Joe Wilkinson puts base rate in the high 20s to 30 percent of total cost. Refund Retriever's Brian asks for a 98-inch variance on a 97-inch product instead of only a discount.; assumptions note: Additional handling also triggers at 50 pounds; Refund Retriever pushes that definition to 53 or 55 pounds. Glenn Gooding's 20x20x22 inch, 20 lb box jumped 190% ($19.69 to $57.18, zone 5) under the UPS 8,640-cubic-inch rule. DIM divisors in play run 139, 166, 194, and custom 250.; note: Attributed to Refund Retriever (iizNycveRfc, TzPaNZCC4js, v9AT9Omrd5c), iDrive Logistics (H64bWcLI0O8), S3 Stores (q9kvSNRcgfs), Amware Fulfillment (d3jQIelSHJM), and Experidium (8-Sguow2LDM), whose rerate surfaced 2.38% of audited spend.
